sentences.text:
Vijay Singh Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10
October, 2022
Bench: Hemant Gupta, B.V. Nagarathna

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. 1738 Of 2022
 [@ Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 8637 Of 2022]
 Vijay Singh Dhakad Ap
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Re
 O R D E R
Leave granted.

The challenge in the present appeal is to an order passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh,
Bench at Gwalior, on 15.03.2022, whereby a revision filed by the appellant against his conviction for an offence under Section 16(1)a(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was not interfered with.
The allegation against the appellant was that though the amount of fat in the sample of Milk was found to be sufficient at 5.5%, but the amount of solids not fat was found to be at lower end at 7.365% in place of 8.5%.
The appellant has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year and fine of Rs. 1000/-.

entities.text:
High Court of Madhya Pradesh,
Bench at Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has pointed out that the appellant Reason: has already undergone 7 months and 22 days of imprisonment, apart from the fact that the appellant has faced the prosecution for almost 20 years.
The minimum sentence imposable under the Act is three months.
In view of the said fact, the sentence imposed upon the appellant is reduced to that already undergone.
With the above modification in the sentence, the appeal stands disposed of.
The appellant be released from jail forthwith, if not required in any other case.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of.
